scope_note: Provisional discovery and gap-closure account for Meta's multi-building Fort Worth data-center campus and the selected 634,395-square-foot IM3 footprint. Winner LLC records at 4500 Like Way, later lot references at 5000 Like Way, and campus-wide operator disclosures are retained as unallocated campus evidence because no public crosswalk maps the inventory footprint to the Building 3, Building 4.2, Building 5-6, or FTW4 identifiers. The proposed Winner retrofit at 14100 Park Vista is excluded because current official QTS material continues to identify that address as the separate QTS Fort Worth campus. Exact observations, administrative permit estimates, conditional projections, overlapping cumulative totals, assessment bases, recipient grants, tax-abatement beneficiaries, and infrastructure payments remain separate; no modeled synthesis is justified at this handoff.

project_updates.title: Identity, boundary and chronology
project_updates.notes: Meta broke ground in 2015 and reports the Fort Worth campus operational since 2017; continuous construction and TDLR phases extend the chronology through the 2022 FTW4 schedule and a 2023 small retrofit search result. Address, lot, operator, SEC subsidiary, assessor and permit searches support a Winner/Meta campus boundary at 4500/5000 Like Way, but not an individual-building allocation.
project_updates.project_description: Meta Fort Worth is Meta’s multi-building data-center campus at 4500 Like Way in north Fort Worth, Tarrant County, operated through Winner LLC. Winner broke ground in 2015 and the campus began operating in 2017; public audit and permit records trace later buildings, utilities and retrofit phases through 2023. The selected IM3 object is one 634,395-square-foot mapped footprint, but public records do not crosswalk it to Meta’s Building 3, 4.2, 5-6 or FTW4 identifiers, so campus totals remain unallocated and the separate QTS campus at 14100 Park Vista Boulevard is excluded.

project_updates.title: Winner LLC operator crosswalk
project_updates.notes: SEC subsidiary exhibits list Winner LLC under Meta, while TDLR, Fort Worth audit, appraisal and tax-abatement sources connect Winner to 4500 Like Way and the Facebook/Meta project. Company-wide SEC financials were searched but contain no Fort Worth investment, revenue, payroll, tax, utility or community allocation.

project_updates.title: Adjacent QTS boundary exclusion
project_updates.notes: Tarrant agreement, permit, appraisal, operator and archive searches found Winner's proposed 2019 retrofit at 14100 Park Vista, but current QTS material still identifies that address as QTS FTW1. No deed, completion, ownership or operating crosswalk was found, so the QTS site and its power, area, cooling and equipment figures are excluded.

project_updates.title: Assessor, tax roll and bill search
project_updates.notes: Tarrant Appraisal District owner/address/top-taxpayer, Tarrant tax-office, Truth-in-Taxation, county college and regional water district ACFR routes were searched. The City of Fort Worth tax-unit real and personal property components are retained as one disclosed combined stock; tax-unit totals differ, direct account IDs and a complete annual tax-bill/payment series were not established, and no value was converted into tax receipts.

project_updates.title: City incentives, compliance and payments search
project_updates.notes: Fort Worth Chapter 380 agreement CSC 46728, 2015 tax abatement, 2016 boundary amendment, audit reports, economic-development transparency workbook, council packets, contracts, check register and FY2025 accounts-payable audit were searched. The 2018 audit supports construction observations; a later $14,415,465.40 Winner payment is not retained because the audit table does not identify purpose or account coding, and no complete city grant or abatement payment series was found.

project_updates.title: County incentive and abatement search
project_updates.notes: Tarrant Commissioners Court orders, original and expansion agreements, active-abatement schedule, annual reports and ACFR routes were searched. Only the separately reported 2018 county and hospital-district year-one abatements are retained; later Winner abatements are combined across accounts and phases and therefore remain unallocated.

project_updates.title: State incentive, exemption and financing search
project_updates.notes: Texas Comptroller certified-data-center, tax-exemption, Chapter 313 and transparency routes plus Texas Enterprise Fund, bond, TIF and public-financing searches were checked for Winner, Ernst, Facebook, Meta, 4500 Like Way and 14100 Park Vista. Certification is retained as context, but no realized state exemption, TEF award, Chapter 313 benefit, public bond proceeds, grant or TIF amount was identified.

project_updates.title: Planning, permit and phase search
project_updates.notes: Fort Worth issued-permit reports, development portal, Certificates of Occupancy references, TDLR TABS and archived construction reporting were searched by Winner, Project Ernst, FTW, address, lot and contractor. Four major TDLR estimated-cost observations are retained as source projections without summation; local permits also show later electrical, fire-water and retrofit work but no complete non-overlapping permit ledger or IM3 crosswalk.

project_updates.title: Construction workforce and payroll search
project_updates.notes: Operator, DPR/Fortis contractor, audit, permit, council, workforce-board, QCEW and archive searches preserved the existing 1,200-worker historical peak. No annual construction employment, worker residence, hours by phase, wages, payroll, job-years, contractor headcount or apprenticeship completion series was found; third-party averages were rejected.

project_updates.title: Supplier and local-spend search
project_updates.notes: Audit invoices, pay applications, vendor-address verification, contractor announcements, procurement, M/WBE, council and vendor-payment routes were searched. The audited $74,215,330 Fort Worth construction-spend observation is retained, but no complete supplier list, supplier ownership, nonconstruction purchasing, local operating spend, annual series or induced supplier employment was found.

project_updates.title: Operations employment and payroll search
project_updates.notes: Meta careers, operator posts, incentive agreements, audit compliance, QCEW, CBP, workforce and archive searches found an observed lower bound of more than 150 people in 2020 and a distinct conditional 200-plus jobs-supported projection. No current direct FTE, payroll, wages, employee residence, occupations, contractor split, training outcomes or indirect/induced job observation was verified.

project_updates.title: Electric utility and grid search
project_updates.notes: Meta energy reports, PUC service-area directories, ERCOT, Oncor, Brazos, AllianceTexas, utility tariffs, substation and council searches were checked for electricity, demand, capacity, bills, rates and company-funded grid work. Only Meta's 2020-2024 facility electricity series is retained; provider identity, customer bills, peak demand, IT load, tariff, substation cost and Fort Worth-specific renewable capacity remain unverified.

project_updates.title: Water, wastewater and reclaimed-water search
project_updates.notes: Fort Worth utility agreements, council records, water and wastewater rates, TWDB, TCEQ, Meta water reports and restoration-benefit reports were searched. The 2.45 MGD agreement figure is capacity, not use; Meta directly reports 2020-2024 withdrawals of 300, 254, 346, 404 and 311 megaliters, but the locked catalog lacks an actual-withdrawal metric, so the series is documented rather than mislabeled as planned use. No consumption, discharge, reclaimed-water volume, bill or selected-building allocation was found.

project_updates.title: Environmental and generator search
project_updates.notes: TCEQ air application, permit, emission-event, stormwater and compliance routes plus EPA ECHO and operator environmental reports were searched for Alliance Site, Winner, Meta and 4500 Like Way. Location-based and market-based scope 2 values are outside the locked catalog, and no stable generator count, fuel use, operating hours, actual criteria emissions, discharge or violation amount was retained.

project_updates.title: Community recipient confirmation search
project_updates.notes: Operator grant lists, school, museum, Nature Center, nonprofit, city budget, council and local-news archives were searched. Three museum grants are recipient-confirmed and retained inside the non-additive $5.2 million-plus county-area total; a $300,000 Nature Center commitment and other named recipients lacked equally clear payment evidence or complete annual coverage and were not inserted.

project_updates.title: Infrastructure and public-service cost search
project_updates.notes: City capital plans, water developer agreements, council awards, fire, police, roads, emergency management, budget, ACFR, bond and service-cost searches retained Winner's $879,851.31 water-main payment. No marginal recurring public-service cost, city-funded project share attributable to Meta, road subsidy, emergency-response cost, net fiscal balance or break-even observation was found.

project_updates.title: County outcome source audit
project_updates.notes: The governed Tarrant panel contains complete 2001-2024 BEA real GDP, BLS QCEW covered employment and weekly wage, and Census population context. CBP and QCEW industry routes were also searched, but county and industry aggregates do not isolate Meta, suppliers, commuters or the selected building.

project_updates.title: County GDP, employment and wage model dispositions
project_updates.notes: study.modeled_county_gdp_comparison_gap — rejected because treatment could be 2015 groundbreaking, 2017 service start or later continuous expansions and no defensible donor set or isolated shock was established. study.modeled_county_employment_comparison_gap — rejected because continuous construction, the pandemic break, commuting and multiple large employers prevent a unique intervention. study.modeled_county_wage_comparison_gap — rejected because aggregate wages cannot separate Meta workers, construction labor, suppliers or changing industry mix. Descriptive 2001-2024 panel data remain context, not contribution estimates.

project_updates.title: Metric disposition ledger — investment, construction, suppliers and operations
project_updates.notes: study.cumulative_facility_investment retained twice as non-additive current operator and 2015-2017 audited observations; study.construction_peak_workers retained in base evidence; study.permitted_construction_value retained as four distinct TDLR source projections; study.cumulative_local_contractor_spend retained from the city audit; study.operating_employees retained as a 2020 lower-bound snapshot; study.operational_jobs_supported retained as a conditional projection. Annual investment, verified phase expenditure, construction payroll/job-years, operating payroll/residence, supplier ownership and operating purchases remain unavailable and unmodeled.

project_updates.title: Metric disposition ledger — fiscal and public costs
project_updates.notes: study.account_assessed_value retained for the 2024 City of Fort Worth tax-unit combined roll; study.infrastructure_company_payments retained for the actual water-main receipt; study.local_property_tax_credits retained as separate 2018 county and hospital-district abatements. Property-tax receipts, direct taxes, annual city Chapter 380 grants, realized state sales-tax exemption, utility service payments, public debt, service costs and net fiscal results remain unavailable and unmodeled.

project_updates.title: Metric disposition ledger — resources and community
project_updates.notes: study.annual_electricity_use retained for 2020-2024; actual water withdrawal is directly observed but omitted because no matching locked metric exists; renewable capacity is statewide and excluded; generator count, demand, bills, wastewater and resource costs remain unavailable. study.cumulative_community_funding and three study.direct_community_contribution records are retained with nesting warnings; no complete recipient or annual giving ledger is claimed.

project_updates.title: Legal, court, archive and adverse search
project_updates.notes: SEC EDGAR, Texas and Tarrant court/order indexes, Fort Worth contracts and agendas, public-record archives, operator archives and news searches used Winner, Ernst, Facebook, Meta, Like Way, Park Vista, permit, tax, water, utility, supplier, payroll, bond and lawsuit terms. No project-specific judgment, settlement, enforcement payment, public bond, hidden ownership transfer or evidence sufficient to reverse the QTS exclusion was identified; absence is not asserted as zero.

project_updates.title: Provisional handoff status
project_updates.notes: candidate_pending_adversarial_review. Discovery and distinct gap-closure are complete for the documented source families, but this first handoff is not finally accepted: independent adversarial corrective review must challenge the boundary, page-image transcription, tax-unit/account mapping, city payment coding, water metric-catalog gap, overlap controls and the decision to retain no models.
